messages:
maya-customer: Hey @support — after switching to structured JSON mode our parser is failing intermittently.

maya-customer: We see numbers like "12345" and booleans like "false" instead of 12345 / false. Also some enums come back as "Enabled" vs schema expects "enabled". Here's the API call and a sample response.

maya-customer: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
    "input": "Generate user payload",
    "structured_output": {
      "format": "json_schema",
      "schema": {
        "type":"object",
        "properties": {
          "user_id": {"type":"number"},
          "is_active": {"type":"boolean"},
          "plan": {"type":"string","enum":["free","paid","enterprise"]}
        },
        "required":["user_id","is_active","plan"]
      },
      "mode":"strict"
    },
    "temperature": 0.2
  }'
```

maya-customer: sample response body from the API (we get HTTP 200, but downstream JSON parse fails):

maya-customer: ```json
{
  "user_id": "12345",
  "is_active": "false",
  "plan": "Enabled"
}
```

anna-support: Thanks @maya — this looks like a strict-mode validation / coercion problem. Can you paste the request_id from the response headers (x-request-id)? Also which SDK / version are you using?

maya-customer: request-id: r-3f9a2b7, using python-sdk v0.8.2

liam-engineer: looping in @eng-runtime-bot and @anna-support. Error text when we run the validator locally: `TypeMismatchError: field user_id expected number but got string`. The enum casing mismatch would also fail strict mode because `Enabled` != `enabled`.

liam-engineer: quick repro I ran locally with same schema — the model sometimes emits quotes around numbers at temp>0. Also some fine-tuned outputs include Title-case enums. Two mitigation paths:
- short-term: set `structured_output.coerce_types = true` or disable `mode: "strict"`.
- short-term (prompt-level): set `temperature: 0` and `top_p: 0` and include an explicit instruction to emit raw numbers/booleans.

liam-engineer: Example immediate workaround (curl):

liam-engineer: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
    "input": "Generate user payload. Output must be strictly JSON: numbers without quotes, booleans as true/false, enum lowercase.",
    "structured_output": {"format":"json_schema","schema":{...},"mode":"strict","coerce_types":true},
    "temperature": 0,
    "top_p": 0
  }'
```

anna-support: @maya can you try the same call with `coerce_types:true` and temp 0? If that works we'll keep you on that config while we investigate.

eng-runtime-bot: Incident INC-2024-234 opened: structured-output-type-drift. Assigned: @liam-engineer. ETA initial triage 60m.

maya-customer: Tried coerce_types + temp 0 — looks much better, downstream parser accepted the response. Thanks.

liam-engineer: Root cause summary: in strict mode our validator refuses to coerce (intended), but the model can emit quoted numbers/enums with inconsistent casing when temperature > 0 or when certain prompt tokens bias output. We'll push a patch to allow a server-side `coerce_types` opt-in and improve the canonicalization of enums on model output. Tracking in INC-2024-234.

anna-support: Closing loop: for now we recommend customers use `coerce_types:true` or `mode: "lax"` if they can't lock temp to 0. We'll add this guidance to the support KB.

maya-customer: Appreciated, please tag me when fixed in prod.

liam-engineer: Will do — adding steps to the incident with logs and exact reproducer. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
